identity.title: Anomalously Narrow Line Widths of Compact Massive Star-forming Galaxies at z ∼ 2.3: A Possible Inclination Bias in the Size-Mass Plane

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present ALMA observations of the CO(3-2) emission line of three compact, massive galaxies with H$\alpha$ line widths of FWHM(H$\alpha$)$\sim$125-260 km s$^{-1}$ to test this hypothesis.

question.value: Are the narrow Halpha line widths of compact massive star-forming galaxies at z~2.3 due to dust obscuration of high-velocity central gas? Measured via CO(3-2) line widths.

evidence.quote: We used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to observe three galaxies at $z \sim 2.3$ from the vD15 sample that have very small H$\alpha$ line widths
as part of ID: 2018.1.01841.S program
The observations were carried out in Band-3 using four spectral windows covering the rest-frame frequency range of $304-349$ GHz.
We robustly detect the CO $J=3-2$ emission line in all three galaxies
in array configuration C43-3 (shortest and longest baselines were 15 and 1240 m, respectively)
shortest and longest baselines were 15 and 1240 m, respectively
The synthesized beam sizes are $\sim 1.2\mu{''}\times1.2\mu{''}$
the rms levels are 0.20–0.25 mJy/beam over 50 km s$^{-1}$ in the channel maps
The on-source integration times were $30-42$ minutes

findings_qualitative.value: CO line widths are similar to or narrower than Halpha, ~3x smaller than virial expectation; dust obscuration hypothesis rejected; face-on disks and inclination bias in the size-mass plane proposed

evidence.quote: These results show that the narrow H$\alpha$ linewidths of many compact massive star-forming galaxies are not due to preferential obscuration of the highest velocity gas.

claims.hypothesis: Narrow Halpha widths result from dust obscuration of high-velocity central gas
claims.experiment: ALMA CO(3-2) observations of three compact massive SFGs

evidence.quote: We conclude that we can reject the hypothesis that the narrow H$\alpha$ lines in these objects were the result of preferential attenuation of the gas with the highest velocities.

claims.hypothesis: There is an inclination bias in the size-mass plane
claims.experiment: Compare size and axis ratio for massive SFGs
claims.result: Anti-correlation between size and axis ratio
claims.finding: Face-on galaxies may appear more compact; not conclusive

evidence.quote: Although not conclusive, this hypothesis is supported by an observed anti-correlation between size and axis ratio of massive galaxies.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Different CO transition tracing different gas; central regions devoid of gas (quenched centers) - second judged hard to reconcile with UV-optical morphology and SEDs

evidence.quote: However, it is difficult to reconcile with the rest-frame UV–optical morphology and spectral energy distributions of the galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Beam (~1.2") large compared to galaxy sizes, so spatially resolved kinematics inconclusive for two galaxies

evidence.quote: Nothing conclusive can be said about either C1 or G5 and extent of the gas.
